title: Henry Pritchett and his Tonic Triad band
summary: Clark recalls Henry Pritchett, who organised a thirty-piece concert band, and gives his address and tailor shop. His Tonic Triad band won every prize at Hot Springs in 1929.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You still live down there near St. Bernard someplace?
Yeah. Yeah. He lives on 1712 St. Louis. That's near St. Louis Cemetery. Yeah.
Oh we're looking him up. I see.
Yeah he's a tailor. He has a shop on South Ramport there. I think 222 and a half.
I thought he lived way down in Louisville.
No he lived 1712 St. Louis. I mean St. Louis near Claiborne.
He's right next to Johnny's Music. That's right.
Right next door to Johnny's Music. You told me about him he is. That's right.
You ought to go down and talk with him.
What was his band called? Tonic Triad. He took that band to Hot Springs, Arkansas in 29 and won every prize there was. Every prize there was we won it.
